question: Could you give me the background on the war this treaty ended? The handout assumes we already know and I missed that lesson.
field_atlas_2b:
The war ended by the Treaty of Münster and the Treaties of Osnabrück and Münster in October 1648, which concluded the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire. The negotiations began in 1643 and were conducted from 1643 to 1648 in two towns in Westphalia: Catholic delegations met in Münster and Protestant delegations met in Osnabrück [S2]. The treaty recognized Dutch independence following the Treaty of Münster signed in January 1648, which ended the Eighty Years' War [S1]. It also recognized the principle of cuius regio, eius religio, confirming Calvinism alongside Catholicism and Lutheranism, while the "normal year" of 1624 was used to determine which territories counted as Catholic or Protestant [S1]. The treaty ended the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire [S1], recognized Switzerland's independence from the Empire [S3], and granted German princes the right to make alliances with foreign powers as long as they were not against the Emperor [S1]. Additionally, Sweden gained Western Pomerania and Bremen-Verden, while France gained most of Alsace and confirmed control of Metz, Toul, and Verdun [S1]. Historians link the treaty to the idea of state sovereignty because it was one of the first great European peace congresses, though some argue it kept the Holy Roman Empire together and gave outside powers the right to guarantee the settlement [S3].

_Based on 1 of 6 passages from f06.txt, chosen for this question; the rest of the file was not used._
reference: A KZG commitment is a short cryptographic fingerprint of your blob, computed by treating the blob's 4096 field elements as the evaluations of a polynomial and committing to that polynomial as a single 48-byte BLS12-381 point, using a trusted setup produced by the KZG ceremony. Its value is that anyone can later be given one evaluation plus a small proof and verify it against the commitment, which is what precompile 0x0A does. The versioned hash is how the EVM refers to that commitment cheaply: 0x01 as a version byte followed by the last 31 bytes of sha256 of the commitment, which is what your type-3 transaction actually carries, since the blobs themselves never enter the EVM. On PeerDAS: nodes stop downloading whole blobs and instead sample erasure-coded columns, so no single node necessarily holds complete blobs. Your archiver therefore cannot assume it can fetch full blobs from any peer, and should keep pulling complete blobs from a supernode or your own full-blob node.

reference: Autolyse is just flour plus water, rested before salt and levain go in. During that rest the flour hydrates fully, and the enzymes already in the flour get to work: protease relaxes the gluten so it stretches instead of tearing, and amylase starts turning damaged starch into sugars the yeast can use. The result is a smoother, more extensible dough with less kneading, which is why you add salt later, since salt tightens gluten and slows those enzymes. Hydration of 75% is baker's percentage: water as a percentage of total flour weight. You have 500 g flour and 375 g water, so 375/500 = 75%. Everything else in your recipe is quoted the same way: 2% salt is 10 g, 20% levain is 100 g. Higher hydration gives a more open, custardy crumb but slacker dough that is harder to shape and less forgiving of over-proofing, so stepping to 80% means roughly 400 g water and expecting a looser dough.

reference: In plain terms: as we age, some cells stop dividing but refuse to die. These senescent cells are few, but they leak a cocktail of inflammatory signals (the SASP) that irritates the tissue around them, and they pile up in arthritic joints, furred arteries, scarred lung and fat tissue. Mouse work with the INK-ATTAC model showed that deliberately killing these cells from mid-life delays age-related decline and extends median lifespan, which is the proof of principle. Senescent cells survive by switching on anti-apoptotic pathways, so drugs that block those pathways kill them selectively: the leukaemia drug dasatinib plus the plant compound quercetin, navitoclax (potent but drops platelet counts), and fisetin. Because the cells take weeks to return, these are given in short intermittent courses. Human evidence is still thin: small pilots in lung fibrosis and diabetic kidney disease were encouraging but tiny, and a Phase 2 knee osteoarthritis trial of UBX0101 missed its endpoint. Key unknowns are how to measure senescent burden in people and whether clearance harms wound healing.

TA-65 is a cycloastragenol-based supplement; the published human studies are small, short, partly industry-funded and measure leukocyte telomere length, not lifespan or disease. reference: Air below freezing still holds plenty of heat, because "cold" only means cold relative to your house, not empty of energy; even at -2 C the air is nearly 271 degrees above absolute zero. A heat pump moves that heat rather than making any. A refrigerant such as the R290 in your quote is expanded through a valve so its boiling point drops well below the outside air temperature, perhaps -20 C. Outside air blown over the evaporator is then warmer than the refrigerant, so heat flows the natural way and boils it to vapour. The compressor squeezes that vapour, which raises its pressure and temperature above your 45 C flow temperature, and in the indoor heat exchanger it condenses, giving the heat up to your water. Electricity only drives the compressor and fans, which is why output exceeds input. Efficiency falls as it gets colder and during defrost cycles, which is what your 40 litre volumiser and the -2.3 C design temperature are there to handle.

question: what do donepezil and memantine actually do, and are they two of the same thing?
field_atlas_2b:
Donepezil and memantine are distinct medications with different mechanisms of action; they are not two of the same thing. Donepezil is a cholinesterase inhibitor that increases the levels of acetylcholine in the brain to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease [S1]. Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist that regulates glutamate levels in the brain to treat symptoms of dementia [S1]. Both medications are used in the treatment of dementia, but they target different neurotransmitter systems and do not function identically [S1].

VO2max measures the maximum rate of oxygen consumption during incremental exercise, quantified in mL/kg/min, which reflects the body's peak aerobic capacity [S1]. There are two thresholds rather than one because VO2max itself is a single value representing the absolute maximum, while the presence of two thresholds (VT1 and VT2) indicates the existence of a "threshold" (or ventilatory threshold) where the body's metabolic demand exceeds its supply, forcing a shift from aerobic to anaerobic metabolism [S2]. reference: VO2max is the maximum rate at which your body can take in, transport and use oxygen during hard exercise, and because fat and carbohydrate are burned aerobically it effectively caps your sustainable power. It is reported per kilogram of body weight, mL/kg/min, because in running you carry yourself, so a heavier person needs more absolute oxygen for the same pace. Yours of 31.4 is around average for 58. There are two thresholds because two things break down at different intensities. The first, VT1 at 128 bpm for you, is where lactate and ventilation first rise above baseline and breathing deepens; below it you can go for hours, which is why your Z2 work sits there. The second, VT2 or the respiratory compensation point at 152 bpm, is the highest intensity where lactate production and clearance still balance, roughly 30-60 minutes of effort. Economy matters because it decides what fraction of your VO2max a given pace costs, and it improves with training even when VO2max plateaus.
